newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran tells Bonn not to meddle in journalist's case.
newsitem.headline: Iran tells Bonn not to meddle in journalist's case.

text.p: Iranian President Akbar Hashemi Rafsanjani on Wednesday urged Germany not to interfere in the case of an Iranian journalist arrested on charges of attempting to leave the country illegally.

"The issue of (Faraj) Sarkuhi is a one hundred percent domestic issue and the Germans must not interfere in it," the official Iranian news agency IRNA, monitored by the British Broadcasting Corporation, quoted Rafsanjani as telling a news conference in Tehran.
Bonn has asked Tehran to explain reports that Sarkuhi had been detained and tortured for 47 days last year when he was supposedly in Germany, and that he had now been arrested again.
German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel said on Wednesday Bonn was doing its utmost to investigate the case.
Iran has told Bonn that Sarkuhi, editor of the Iranian monthly magazine Adineh (Friday), was arrested in southwest Iran on February 2 while trying to leave the country illegally.
Rafsanjani said Iran found Germany's response to the Sarkuhi case "surprising and confusing".

"We're doing everything to clear up this case," Kinkel told German Radio. "I've sent two letters to (Iranian Foreign Minister Ali Akbar) Velayati. He said he wouldn't allow any interference. I told him this could not be classed as interference as Sarkuhi's wife and children are in Germany."
Kinkel said the European Union's "troika" of the current president -- the Netherlands -- and its immediate predecessor and successor was also pursuing the case.

Iran's relationship with Germany -- Tehran's biggest trading partner -- have become strained in recent months by a pending German court decision on the 1992 killings of three Kurdish dissidents and their translator in a Berlin restaurant.
